p:cNvPr.descr: An image of oxidation of propionyl-CoA produced by beta oxidation of odd-number fatty acids. This image begins with propionyl-CoA, where H bonds down to C, which bonds left and right to H and down to C, which bonds left and right to H, and down to C. C double bonds down and right to O and down and left to CoA-S. Below this is an arrow, represented as propionyl-CoA carboxylase (in blue). To the right of the arrow is a curved arrow that begins at HCO3- (in red) that merges into another curved arrow that begins with ATP and points to ADP [plus] Pi. Inside that arrow is biotin (in red). Below this is d-methylmalonyl-CoA, which begins with H bonding down to C, which bonds left and right to H and down to C. C bonds right to H and down to C, which double bonds down and right to O and down and left to CoA-S. The second C also bonds left to C, which double bonds down and left to O and up and right to –O (C, O, and –O are all in red). Below this are reversible arrows, represented as methylmalonyl-CoA epimerase (in blue). Below this is L-methylmalonyl-CoA, where H bonds down with C, which bonds left to H (in red box), right to H and down to C. C bonds right to H and left to C, which double bonds up and left to O and down to CoA-S (C, O, and CoA-S are all in a blue box). The second C also bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to O and down and left to –O (C, O, and –O are all in pink). To the right of this are reversible arrows with coenzyme B12 in pink on top and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase in blue below. To the right of the arrows is succinyl-CoA, where C double bonds up and left to O and down and left to CoA-S (all in a blue box), and bonds right to C, which bonds up and right to H, and down to C, which bonds left to H (in pink box) and right to H, and down to C. This C double bonds down and right to O and down and left to –O (all in pink).
